A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGE research, with matching methods, datasets and substantial retained content. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete supporting information are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, calibration, uncertainty-ranking and OOD experiments, together with timing measurements and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical experiments and adds computational scaling measurements, additional uncertainty results and an OOD score-distribution analysis.

M1.justification: The exponential variance gate, normalized member predictions, VGMU score, training objective and gradient procedure remain unchanged. v2 clarifies component applicability and inputs; the analytical gradient appendix S2 is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, including SVHN-to-CIFAR-10 OOD detection. The added synthetic timing sweep varies ensemble and class dimensions without adding a predictive dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: The uncertainty-quality comparators remain EU, EPKL and EPJS, and DE already appears in v1's appendix comparisons. However, v2's measured runtime comparison includes EPJS and EU alongside EPKL; v1's numerical timing comparison reports only EPKL.

E3.justification: The single CIFAR-100 timing example on an Apple M3 Pro is replaced by a systematic synthetic-output benchmark on an RTX 4090, using 128 samples per configuration and crossing M={2,5,10,20,50,100} with C={10,100,1000}. This substantially expands the efficiency evaluation protocol. The predictive training and OOD protocols are essentially retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic runtime scaling analysis over ensemble size and class count, plus Figure S8's EPKL density analysis investigating worsening ID/OOD overlap. These extend the analysis of computational behavior and detection failures. The fixed-versus-learned k ablation, margin-variance geometry and head/sampling analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report predictive results as mean ± standard deviation over three training seeds. v2 introduces a descriptive effect-size threshold, difference in means divided by the larger standard deviation, for highlighting Tables 3–5, and specifies ten trials for its timing study. Neither establishes increased training repetitions or formal significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds rank/concentration entries, the timing grid in Tables 7/S7 and density findings in Figure S8. Most earlier predictive and OOD results remain. Some redisplayed values conflict: Table 5 gives CIFAR-100 LLE-VGN M=10 accuracy as 0.548 ± 0.014, whereas Table S6 retains v1's 0.545 ± 0.014. The replacement timings use different conditions and do not establish a cross-version performance gain.

T1.justification: New Appendix S7 supplies propositions and claimed proofs for axioms A0–A5, including an A5 convergence guarantee. A3 changes from fully satisfied in v1 Table 4 to partially satisfied in v2 Table 8 because TU monotonicity is excluded. Sensitivity propositions are also revised to acknowledge saturation-dependent modulation; the original gradient derivations remain.

C1.justification: The three principal VGE/VGMU/VGN contributions remain. v2 qualifies the abstract's 'matches or exceeds' claim and explicitly limits competitiveness to the evaluated controlled settings, positioning the method as a computationally efficient complement without uniform performance gains.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly restricts training-time VGN to separately trainable DE/LLE members and expands limitations to tail-class shifts, full-posterior calibration and class-dependent error costs. It replaces the earlier diversity-based explanation of EPKL degradation with score-distribution overlap analysis and qualifies A3 compliance. These materially refine applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: The new timing study identifies an RTX 4090, Intel i9-13900KF, 32 GB RAM and its sample configuration, replacing the earlier Mac timing disclosure. Appendix S3's architecture, optimizer, dropout, early stopping and numerical-stability details are essentially unchanged, as is code access.

R1.justification: The moment-based discussion replaces Malinin and Gales (2018) with Smith and Gal (2018), also drawing on the already-cited Depeweg et al. (2018). v2 more explicitly positions VGMU as complementary to information-theoretic measures, while retaining the principal prior-work landscape.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the introduction's Bayesian and entropy exposition into Background and Related Work subsections, expands component explanations and design rationale, rewrites the forward/backward walkthrough, creates a dedicated efficiency subsection and revises the concluding narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds a framework overview, runtime plots and an OOD density figure; redraws the computational graph; introduces component, applicability, complexity and proof-summary tables; and expands main result tables with ensemble-size groups and statistical highlighting. Much calibration content is redisplayed from existing appendix tables rather than newly generated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition, documents efficiency more systematically and qualifies performance and applicability claims. However, its new axiomatic proofs introduce substantive reliability concerns: S7.5 assumes a uniform gate despite class-dependent k and s, while S7.6 claims normalized predictions return to the original predictions as k grows, contrary to the stated gate's generally unequal limiting class weights. These reporting gains and unsupported formal guarantees prevent a reliable judgment of the net effect on quality.
